title: How trains work
examples: What is the difference between steam and electric trains?
How do trains move without wheels touching the ground?
Can you show me a picture of a train engine?

explain.say: Trains need a way to make power to move.

items: Steam uses hot water and steam.
Diesel uses oil burned in an engine.

explain.say: Steam trains use boiling water to create steam power.
Diesel trains use a diesel engine that burns oil.

items: Fuel Tank: Holds the diesel oil

explain.say: Electric trains get their power from overhead wires.
Maglev trains float above the tracks using magnets.
All trains need rails and wheels to run smoothly.

draw.text: Rails and Wheels: The basic track

faq.q: Do all trains use the same kind of power?
faq.a: No, trains use different power sources like steam, diesel, or electricity. Some trains are designed for specific types of tracks.
asks: What different fuels do trains use?
Are there different types of train engines?

faq.q: How does a maglev train work without wheels?
faq.a: Maglev trains use powerful magnets to lift and push them above the track. This floating reduces friction greatly.

faq.q: What is the main job of the rails?
faq.a: The rails are the fixed steel tracks that guide the train wheels safely. They keep the train on the correct path.
asks: Why are the tracks so important?
What are the tracks made of?

faq.q: Is steam power still used for trains today?
faq.a: Steam trains are mostly historical now, but they are sometimes used for special events or tourist rides. Modern trains use electricity or diesel.
asks: Can I see a real steam train?

faq.a: A locomotive is the engine car that pulls the rest of the train carriages. It contains the main power source.
asks: Is the engine always at the front?

facts: Steam engines use the expansion of steam to create motion.
Diesel engines burn fuel inside an engine to create power.
Electric trains draw power from overhead wires using a pantograph.
Maglev trains use magnetic levitation to float above the track.

quiz.say: A train that uses oil burned in an engine is most likely a:
quiz.why: Diesel trains use oil, which is a liquid fuel burned in an engine.

wrong.0: Electric trains need wires to carry the power to them.
wrong.1: Maglev trains use magnets to float, not oil.
wrong.3: Steam uses boiling water, not oil, for its power.

quiz.say: If a train uses power from wires above it, it is:
quiz.why: Electric trains connect to overhead wires to draw the necessary electrical power.

wrong.1: Steam power comes from boiling water in a boiler.
wrong.2: Diesel power comes from burning diesel oil in an engine.
wrong.3: Maglev trains use magnets to lift and move.

quiz.say: The main function of the rails and wheels together is to:
quiz.why: The rails guide the wheels, and the wheels provide the necessary contact for movement.

wrong.0: Floating is done by magnets, not just wheels on rails.
wrong.1: Burning fuel is the engine's job, not the track's job.
wrong.2: Steam generation happens in a separate boiler unit.
